items.title: Investors in Anticipation Over Musk’s Next Big SpaceX Deal
items.summary: Ahead of SpaceX’s quarterly earnings report, many on Wall Street are wondering whether Elon Musk will combine it with Tesla.
items.full_text:
Title: Investors in Anticipation Over Musk’s Next Big SpaceX Deal - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/20/business/dealbook/musk-spacex-deal-tesla.html

Published Time: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:43:47 GMT

Markdown Content:
Image

Image

![Image 1: Elon Musk, left, in a suit, holding a medal with President Trump.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/10/20/multimedia/20db-musk-wgvh/20db-musk-wgvh-articleLarge.jpg?quality=75&auto=avif&disable=upscale)

Investors and analysts will probably press Elon Musk, left, about SpaceX’s spending on artificial intelligence — and whether he might seek to combine the company with Tesla.Credit...Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times

**Andrew here.**How high can energy prices go without hurting the stock market? Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, topped $110 a barrel this morning, yet surprisingly — unless you believe that strong corporate earnings mean energy costs don’t matter — the stock market has stayed calm.

But if oil stays here or climbs higher, companies’ bottom lines could get squeezed. We’re focusing on earnings this week, as heavyweights like Netflix, G.M. and United Airlines report, as well as SpaceX, which we get into below.

## Big questions about SpaceX

When SpaceX reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, there will be plenty of things for Wall Street to keep an eye on.

Investors and analysts will study **Elon Musk**’s trillion-dollar colossus over its artificial intelligence spending. And then there’s the question of whether Musk will announce a long-awaited combination of SpaceX with Tesla (which reports earnings on Wednesday).

**SpaceX is increasingly an A.I. story.**Tech stocks went up on Monday, as investors appeared to set aside their worries about the scale and speed of the A.I. buildout. Companies like Anthropic have continued to demonstrate a [hunger for computing power](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-19/nscale-anthropic-in-talks-for-45-billion-cloud-computing-deal) — a need that SpaceX is betting on by building huge, and hugely expensive, data centers.

Last quarter, SpaceX’s A.I. spending exploded to $15.8 billion in the quarter, more than double its previous quarterly outlay.

Wall Street watchers are less concerned about whether SpaceX can get the financing than about [how much doing so will cost](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-earnings-preview-ai-spending-annual-recurring-revenue-now-becoming-the-bigger-story-162610825.html), Adam Jonas, an analyst at Morgan Stanley, wrote in a recent research note.

**Also watch Starlink,** the satellite internet service that generates a majority of SpaceX’s revenue. Analysts will look to see whether the business is still growing strongly, after revenue rose 66 percent year on year last quarter.

SpaceX recently battered U.S. telecom stocks with its deal to [buy billions of dollars’ worth of wireless spectrum](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/spacexs-spectrum-deal-still-leaves-it-far-rivaling-telecom-giants-2026-10-16/), raising the prospect of it offering cellular phone service. But it also faces challenges in Europe: Several telecom companies there announced plans to explore creating a [satellite mobile phone service](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-19/europe-s-top-carriers-explore-satellite-group-to-fend-off-spacex).

*   Pay attention to what Musk says about Ukraine, after **Volodymyr Zelensky**, the country’s president, complained about his forces’ [access to the military version of Starlink](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/17/zelensky-starlink-elon-musk-trump). Musk recently declared that it’s “[time for Zelensky to go](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2110557192650641827).”

**What about a Tesla tie-up?** Investors have long speculated that Musk would seek to [unite the two companies](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/17/business/spacex-tesla-merger-elon-musk.html), as he has done [again](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/03/business/dealbook/spacex-xai-merger.html) and [again](https://www.nytimes.com/2016/11/18/business/dealbook/tesla-and-solarcity-shareholders-approve-merger.html).

Some on Wall Street have speculated whether that transaction [could be announced](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/will-spacex-merge-with-tesla-speculation-resurfaces-it-could-happen-before-the-end-of-2026-162443386.html) before year end. But uniting the two makes sense, Gene Munster, whose Deepwater Asset Management is invested in both companies, told DealBook’s Brian O’Keefe:

> If Elon’s master plan is around A.I., which he’s been talking about forever, then in order to have a true A.I. company, you have to have the physical side, the terrestrial side. It’s like three quarters or half a vision without Tesla.

Image

### HERE’S WHAT’S HAPPENING

**Saudi Arabia postpones its big investment conference.** The Future Investment Initiative Institute said that its annual meeting, which was set to take place next week and feature speakers like **Jamie Dimon** of JPMorgan Chase and **Larry Fink** of BlackRock, would [take place next year](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/business/saudi-investment-fii-houthis.html). The long-awaited move came amid concerns about security, as the Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen [attack Saudi targets](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/12/business/dealbook/saudi-arabia-strikes-energy-airport.html) like an international airport in the kingdom.

**The engineer accused of bugging OpenAI stays in jail.** A federal judge ordered the now-former employee, **Abdulrahman Alfozan**, to [remain in custody without bail](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/technology/saudis-aided-family-openai-engineer.html). Prosecutors accused Alfozan, whom the company accused of planting a recording device in an office, of having extensive ties to the Saudi government; a Saudi Consulate offered to cover Alfozan’s bail, according to his lawyers.

**President Trump says he’s open to meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.** Trump told reporters on Monday that he would [consider meeting his Russian and Chinese counterparts](https://www.wsj.com/world/trump-putin-xi-meeting-ee489ddd) — but about denuclearization, even as Putin suggested that such a gathering would focus on [ending the war in Ukraine](https://www.wsj.com/world/russia/putin-floats-a-summit-with-trump-and-xi-to-decide-ukraines-fate-1cf6acc1). Trump’s apparent [siding with Putin](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/19/us/politics/trump-russia-deals.html) against **Volodymyr Zelensky**, Ukraine’s president, has drawn criticism [even from Republicans](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/19/fallout-trump-russia-energy).

Image

Image

High-end retail shops were among those affected by riots in Paris in recent days.Credit...Matthieu Rondel/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

## Turmoil in France

Calm returned to Paris and other French cities overnight. But investors remain spooked by protests over the weekend that devolved into riots.

Parisians crunched through shards of glasses and burned debris on Tuesday, tallying losses from looted stores and bracing for more demonstrations. Government curfews imposed last night in several neighborhoods emptied cafes usually filled with tourists and locals, deepening a sense of unrest that threatens to spread throughout Europe, Vivienne Walt reports from Paris.

**The latest:**

*   The CAC 40, France’s benchmark stock index, fell, as did other European indexes.

*   Rioters targeted retailers, including the luxury brands [Louis Vuitton and Hermès](https://www.ft.com/content/afaa7a1d-ef43-40ca-a042-4da8de9ff476?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Insurers are expecting at least a [€1 billion hit](https://www.reinsurancene.ws/france-riots-put-srcc-accumulation-risk-in-focus-for-re-insurers-morningstar-dbrs/) from the violence over the weekend, according to Morningstar DBRS.

*   The yield on France’s 10-year government bond rebounded. But Monday’s sell-off pushed the gap between French and German government bond yields — an indicator of Europe’s stability — to a level last seen in 2012.

Image

**European economies have been hit hard.** A cost-of-living crisis and a debt crunch have driven up yields across much of the world since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran sent oil prices skyrocketing.

That, along with Europe’s slow-growth outlook, puts the European Central Bank in a bind.

**France seems especially vulnerable.**One analyst [told Le Point](https://www.lepoint.fr/economie/dette-francaise-les-evenements-du-week-end-renforcent-les-inquietudes-QIQOGNMG3JBH5PJBZQUW4S2G7Y/) that there was a “high” probability that the country’s credit rating would be downgraded as soon as this week.

**European contagion?**There are concerns that the protests — stemming from rising costs and other grievances — could spread to other countries. Demonstrations have occurred in Milan, Brussels and elsewhere in recent days.

Social media accounts associated with the “yellow vest” protest movement in France announced demonstrations for Saturday to express broad anger about rising inflation and stagnant pay.

**Emmanuel Macron appears out of options.**Unlike in previous political crises, Macron, the French president, has little money to throw at the problem, analysts say. France’s debt burden has hit 119 percent of G.D.P., and parliamentarians have feuded for weeks over how to carry out €54 billion ($60.5 billion) in cuts.

Macron, a former investment banker, actively courted international businesses to invest in France.He cannot run in the April presidential election because of term limits — and the turmoil could hand **Marine Le Pen**, the far-right leader whose France-first economic policies have alarmed some economists, a decisive boost in that race.
